rationale: Both candidates independently surface the substance of the single GT concern (trust_remote_code/kernels-version compatibility), correctly noting it was already fixed but the PR body is stale, and both flag the untested new caching path and the red NPU CI gate — strong convergent recall given GT is thin. Y's findings are more rigorously grounded, with exact file:line quotes for CI job definitions (CPU/CUDA/NPU lanes) and a transparent claim-verified/claim-refuted audit trail, making its major test-coverage finding more actionable and trustworthy. X contributes a couple of valid unique points (broad except-clause sticky-failure risk, a speculative kernels>=0.15 dead-code claim) but the latter is less verifiable and slightly weakens precision.
